page_note: No cosmological substrate detectable on this page. The entire page is dedicated to a teaching about the Elect/Catechumen distinction, the seal of faith/knowledge, and the Church as institution. Even the 'horse of a king' simile (segs 14-21) is constructed as a pedagogical analogy directly applied to the catechumen's seal — not a cosmic correspondence but an editorial illustration. Page-level teaching purity is 0.000 (computational pipeline confirms). Heavy ecclesial vocabulary in first half (Elect, Catechumens, freemen, Church) shifts to general analogical material in the second half — but the second half stays within ecclesial frame (catechumen, faith, seal, form). The 'peoples and peoples / heresies' material (segs 5-9) is anti-heretical polemic. Heavy damage (68.8%) but enough survives to determine register clearly.

segments.temporal_note: 'Forms of the entire Church' — explicit ecclesial category.
Direct enumeration of Manichaean two-tier structure: Elect, Catechumens.
Continues 'forms of the Elect and Catechumens' — institutional.
Catechumens, freemen — institutional categories.
Heavily damaged; continues the choosing-the-Elect narrative. With restoration 'he habitually comes downward' — narrative of the apostle's mission.
'Peoples and peoples' (ⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ ⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ) — anti-heretical/anti-pagan polemical register; ⲇⲟⲅⲙⲁ vocabulary.
Restorations supply 'heresies, heresies' — explicit polemic against rival sects. He chooses them by his speech of light = apostolic mission.
'Made them freemen out of the Error of...' — Error (ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ) is polemical category for rival traditions.
'Out of the peoples and works that exist in madness' — polemic against outside religions.
'Attained him in a transformation [ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲣⲣⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ]' — conversion narrative; angels participate. Editorial-mission register.
Angels setting the way to the place of choosing — ecclesial-mission narrative continued.
'Every catechumen — let none of his works...' — institutional rule register.
Gehenna avoided 'on account of the seal of faith' — soteriological/sacramental ecclesial vocabulary.
'Knowledge sealed upon his soul' — sealing language tied to faith institution.
'The manner of a horse of a king' — opens an analogical simile applied pedagogically to the catechumen, not a cosmic correspondence. Maps mundane→ecclesial.
Continuation of the simile: horse sealed with king's seal so none may carry it off — pedagogical illustration, not cosmic mapping.
Continuation: horse cannot be carried into another's house because of the seal.
'In this manner also is that to which the catechumen is likened' — explicit application clause: the simile points at the contemporary catechumen.
Catechumen 'sealed with the seal of the faith' — ecclesial sacramental category.
Continued seal/faith/works ecclesial register.
Pre-conversion works will not lead him to Gehenna — soteriological-institutional.
'His form which they chose from the first... in the upper-place' — though 'upper-place' uses cosmological vocabulary, here it serves the catechumen's institutional form, not a cosmic mapping.
Form personified — applied to catechumen institutional state.
Form trusts in him, does not let his works be defiled — pastoral/institutional teaching.
'Last works he habitually does' — habitual-conversion register, ecclesial.
'On account of his faith' — ecclesial sacramental ground.
First works / form chosen — continuing ecclesial reflection.
'They themselves do not become defiled' — works/form ecclesial register.
Damaged; 'drawn together to a [meeting/place]' — ecclesial-fellowship register.
Angels purifying — though angels are cosmic, here they function in the ecclesial soteriology of the catechumen, not as part of a cosmic mapping.
'You know about this' — direct second-person address; pastoral-didactic voice.
'Inward to the truth, knowledge' — soteriological-ecclesial.
